## Usage (caller’s view)

Install the skill’s locked dependency once, then compare production with the running development branch:

```sh
npm ci --prefix .agents/skills/verify
node .agents/skills/verify/scripts/compare-live.mjs --development http://localhost:5173
node .agents/skills/verify/scripts/compare-live.mjs --development https://preview.example --cases /tmp/subset.json
node --test .agents/skills/verify/scripts/compare-live.test.mjs
```

Production defaults to `https://exposed.today`; an explicit `--production` supports controlled replay tests. Every live invocation prints its new evidence directory and final status. Exit 0 means all selected comparisons succeeded and matched; 1 means differences; 2 means configuration, transport, identity, schema, or evidence-writing errors. Errors take precedence over differences. Equal origins always fail; self-comparison remains a separate manual diagnostic, outside this helper.

The JSON manifest contains only case identities:

```json
{"searches":["unite","west mid","hsbc","john mcdonnell","jahn"],"entities":[{"kind":"funder","query":"BBC","name":"EXACT VERIFIED NAME","funderKind":"EXACT VERIFIED KIND"},{"kind":"member","id":"178","name":"EXACT VERIFIED NAME"}]}
```

Seed funder names/kinds from grounded live results, including grouped BBC, GB News, and Premier League, plus two verified MPs. Unresolved seed identities are errors, never skipped cases.

## Problem

Frozen monetary goldens and local database cloning cannot establish parity with the production users see. The public interface is SvelteKit page data, not `/api/search`. The verifier must decode that interface, preserve money as supplied, resolve environment-specific funder UUIDs independently, and retain enough evidence to distinguish differences from failed observations. It must never change either environment.

## Shape

Keep three skill-owned implementation artifacts: `scripts/compare-live.mjs`, `live-cases.json`, and `scripts/compare-live.test.mjs`, with skill-local `package.json`/lock declaring exact `devalue` 5.9.4. Use Node built-in fetch, filesystem, assertions, and test runner; no frontend imports, browser process, Python decoder, or additional library. JSDoc describes private domain records; runtime parsers enforce them.

```js
// External values become these records only after boundary parsing.
// Amount = decimal-string | null; never Number, arithmetic, or null-to-zero.
// Selector = {kind:'member',id,name} | {kind:'funder',query,name,funderKind}
// SearchRow = {identity, name, kind, funderKind, matchSource}
// Observation = {caseId, normalized, requests:[EvidenceRef]}
// Outcome = matched | different{paths} | error{phase,message,evidence}
async function runComparison(options) { throw Error('not implemented'); }
async function observeCase(instance, caseSpec, evidence) { throw Error('not implemented'); }
function parsePageData(body, expectedRoute) { throw Error('not implemented'); }
function normalizeSearch(model) { throw Error('not implemented'); }
function normalizeDetails(model, selector) { throw Error('not implemented'); }
function compareObservations(production, development) { throw Error('not implemented'); }
```

One script owns wire decoding, selection, projections, and report lifecycle; CLI callers provide only origins and cases. This deep interface hides Svelte/devalue details without spreading one invariant across modules (boundary-discipline, minimize-reader-load).

Each request uses GET, bounded body size, timeout, no redirect following, and sequential execution. Write URL, timestamps, HTTP status, response headers, and untouched body before decoding, including failed HTTP responses. Transport failures retain request metadata. Create a unique run directory before requests; write case outcomes as completed and a final JSON report plus readable path-based diff. Interrupted runs retain raw evidence and an incomplete marker. Origin/build identification is recorded where observable, never invented.

Decode the actual data-node envelope with official `unflatten`; require expected search/detail model, success state, route, and selected identity. A funder selector must match exactly one name/kind in each environment’s search results; fetch each resulting UUID separately. Member routes use Parliament ID plus asserted name. Search projection preserves ordering, duplicate multiplicity, names, entity kinds, funder context, and full match provenance; replace funder UUIDs with name/kind identity while retaining originals in evidence. Member IDs remain significant.

Details project explicit authoritative financial fields: member declared current-term/historical totals, term start, counts/completeness, entry/unknown/undated counts, currencies and category totals; funder currency totals, party totals, recipient identities/totals, entry/unknown counts, and recipient limit. Require every compared field’s expected type; amounts stay exact strings/null. Canonicalize object keys only; preserve array ordering. Never recompute missing totals or accept two error states as equality.

## Synthesis decision

Independent candidate: recommend the single HTTP observer, manifest, and evidence package as the base.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- Accept a pinned decoding dependency for correct framework decoding.
- Accept schema-coupling for explicit fail-closed financial coverage.
- Accept sequential live observations and possible data timing differences for modest production load and clear evidence.

## Alternatives considered

Browser DOM comparison hides decoding but exposes formatting, selectors, and navigation timing while losing exact hidden amounts. Direct Rust API comparison hides frontend details but requires unavailable private routes and fails to verify the public loader. Database snapshots hide network variability but replace the requested live reference with a mutable local fixture.

## Implementation reconciliation

None yet. Tests should replay real-shaped envelopes and mutate amounts, nulls, counts, ordering, identity ambiguity, missing fields, HTTP failures, and duplicate rows. Fixture amounts are test inputs, never live expectations.

## Open questions and risks

Which development URL and verified seed identities will the orchestrator supply? Can live dataset timing explain any observed difference? Report evidence without automatically attributing differences to branch code.

## Next implementation step

Build envelope parsing and exact financial projection with replay tests, then connect the GET/evidence runner and replace frozen-default skill instructions.
# Live comparison design

## Problem

Verification should compare selected search behavior and authoritative totals between one development deployment and `https://exposed.today`. The existing verifier uses a frozen local database and monetary goldens, while production serves SvelteKit page-data encoded with devalue and the Rust API is private. The skill must make bounded read-only GETs, identify corresponding entities across databases, preserve ordered search results and exact financial representations, and emit evidence that distinguishes drift from transport/schema failure. No environment is written or launched.

## Usage (caller's view)

```sh
./.agents/skills/verify/scripts/compare-live.sh \
  --development https://dev.example.test \
  --cases ./.agents/skills/verify/live-cases.json
```

```sh
./.agents/skills/verify/scripts/compare-live.sh --development "$DEV_URL" --cases "$CASES"
# writes runs/<timestamp>/report.json, evidence.jsonl, and report.txt; exits 0 only when all cases match
```

Case manifest contains queries and identity selectors, never expected amounts:

```json
{"searches":["unite","west mid","hsbc","john mcdonnell","jahn","BBC","GBNews","Premier League"],
 "funders":[{"name":"BBC"},{"name":"GB News"}],
 "members":[{"id":178,"name":"John McDonnell"}]}
```

The CLI runs the same requests against both origins, decodes page data, resolves each requested identity, and prints compact field-level differences with report paths for raw evidence.

## Shape

Keep one Node helper as the skill's sole comparison boundary. `compare-live.sh` checks arguments, sets a run directory, and execs `compare-live.mjs`; `package.json` plus lockfile under `scripts/live/` pin direct dependency `devalue` (the SvelteKit wire format decoder) so execution does not depend on frontend `node_modules` or ambient packages. Node built-ins provide fetch, filesystem, and CLI parsing. No browser automation: SSR page-data is the same loader result and avoids selectors/rendering variability.

```ts
type Origin = { label: "development" | "production"; baseUrl: URL };
type CaseManifest = { searches: string[]; funders: FunderSelector[]; members: MemberSelector[] };
type FunderSelector = { name: string };
type MemberSelector = { id: number; name: string };
type SearchHit = { id: string | number; name: string; kind: "MP" | "Funder";
  funderKind: string | null; matchSource: { kind: "name" | "alias"; name?: string } };
type Amount = { currency: string; amount: string | null; entryCount: number; unknownAmountCount: number };
type MemberTotals = { currentTermStart: string; currentTerm: { amount: string; declarationCount: number; incomplete: boolean };
  historical: { amount: string; declarationCount: number; incomplete: boolean }; currencies: Amount[] };
type FunderTotals = { entryCount: number; unknownCurrencyCount: number; recipientLimit: number;
  currencies: Array<Amount & { parties: PartyTotal[]; topRecipients: RecipientTotal[] }> };
type Outcome<T> = { value: T } | { error: { stage: "http"|"decode"|"shape"|"identity"; message: string; url?: string; status?: number } };
```

Public surface is `main(argv): Promise<number>`. Internal functions: `readManifest(path): CaseManifest` (validate nonempty selectors and HTTPS/HTTP origins); `fetchPageData(origin,path): Promise<Outcome<unknown>>` (timeout, GET only, record raw response); `decodeSearch/SearchDetail` (devalue-unflatten and parse required model/status/fields into these types); `resolveFunder(hits, selector): Outcome<SearchHit>` (exact normalized name + Funder kind, exactly one); `compare<T>(path,a,b): Difference[]` (structural comparison retaining array order, exact strings, nulls, counts and booleans); `writeRun(report,evidence): Promise<void>`.

For each query request `/search/__data.json?q=<encoded query>`. For entities, use production-independent resolution on each origin: resolve funder UUID from that origin's search hits, then request `/funders/<id>/__data.json`; member route is `/members/<parliament-id>/__data.json`, and verify returned exact name. Compare hit sequences including duplicates, entity kind, funder kind, match source and alias provenance. Compare member term totals and currency aggregates exactly. Compare funder currency totals, party totals and top recipients, mapping recipients by parliamentary ID plus verified name; omit only transport IDs whose databases legitimately differ (funder UUID).

Failure contract: malformed manifest or origin collision fails before network; every request has a finite timeout and modest sequential execution; non-2xx, invalid devalue, unexpected model/status/shape, missing or ambiguous identity, or absent required financial field is an error with request evidence and nonzero exit. Valid values that differ are reported as differences with nonzero exit, not rewritten into a baseline. Every response records origin, timestamp, URL, status, and raw body; report records both origins, selected normalized values, per-path differences/errors, and exit reason. Strip secrets from URLs; selected endpoints must not contain credentials. Self-comparison is refused, even if explicitly requested.

This surface hides URL construction, SvelteKit/devalue decoding, validation, cross-database identity resolution, exact comparison, and evidence persistence behind one CLI. Callers only provide origins and identity/query cases.

## Synthesis decision

Candidate recommendation: use the official devalue decoder in a skill-owned Node helper. It follows the production wire contract directly and keeps comparison policy in one place.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept pinning a small Node dependency in the skill in exchange for correct SvelteKit decoding without a hand-maintained decoder.
- We accept explicit selected cases instead of scanning every entity in exchange for bounded, repeatable requests and useful evidence.
- We accept treating any selected data difference as a failure in exchange for exposing drift without guessing which environment is wrong.

## Alternatives considered

- Playwright page scraping hides transport decoding but exposes selectors, rendering, and browser setup to the verifier; it is a shallower interface and less stable for exact totals.
- Python plus a custom devalue parser avoids a package install but exposes wire-format complexity in the skill and risks silently misreading future payload variants.
- Frozen monetary goldens provide deterministic expected values but cannot answer whether development matches current production and require ongoing baseline refreshes.

## Implementation reconciliation

No implementation decisions accepted yet.

## Open questions and risks

Should a future manifest support currencies or individual fields to narrow a comparison? Start with whole selected records so omissions remain visible.

## Next implementation step

Build the skill-owned Node package and one fixture-driven helper that decodes the captured production envelope, then wire in live read-only requests and report persistence.

# Live comparison design candidate

## Usage (caller’s view)

Install the skill’s pinned decoder once, then compare against an explicitly supplied development origin:

```sh
npm ci --prefix .agents/skills/verify
node .agents/skills/verify/scripts/compare-live.mjs --development http://localhost:5173
node .agents/skills/verify/scripts/compare-live.mjs --development https://dev.example.test --cases /tmp/selected-cases.json
node --test .agents/skills/verify/scripts/compare-live.test.mjs
```

Production defaults to `https://exposed.today`. Each run prints its evidence directory, counts of matched/different/error cases, and exits 0 only when every case matches; 1 means observed differences, 2 means invalid configuration or incomplete verification. Errors dominate differences. No “update baseline” operation exists.

A manifest contains search queries plus entity selectors, never expected financial values:

```ts
{
  searches: ['unite', 'west mid', 'hsbc', 'john mcdonnell', 'jahn'],
  organisations: [{ query: 'hsbc', name: '<exact observed name>', funderKind: '<observed kind>' }],
  members: [{ id: 178, name: '<exact observed name>' }]
}
```

Seed exact selectors from actual responses; include BBC/GB News/Premier League groups and two MPs where resolvable. Selection failure remains an error, never an automatic skip.

## Problem

Replace a frozen local database/golden comparison with live production versus development observations. Public data is SvelteKit page-data, not the private Rust API. Financial values are already authoritative strings; organisation UUIDs are installation-specific. Verification must distinguish application differences from unavailable or incomparable observations and retain evidence for diagnosis.

## Shape

Use one skill-owned Node module, one manifest, one focused test file, and a skill-local `package.json`/lockfile pinning `devalue` directly. Native fetch, filesystem, crypto, and test runner suffice. Delete the replaced golden helper/refresh workflow so verification has one default path. Keep existing focused application tests.

Sketch (types expressed as JSDoc in `.mjs`):

```ts
type Target = { role: 'production' | 'development'; origin: URL };
type ExactAmount = string | null; // parser accepts decimal strings only; never Number

type EntityIdentity =
  | { kind: 'MP'; id: number; name: string; context: object }
  | { kind: 'Funder'; name: string; funderKind: string };
type SearchRow = { identity: EntityIdentity; matchSource: object };
type Observation =
  | { kind: 'search'; query: string; rows: SearchRow[] }
  | { kind: 'member'; identity: EntityIdentity; totals: object }
  | { kind: 'organisation'; identity: EntityIdentity; totals: object };
type CaseResult =
  | { status: 'match'; caseId: string }
  | { status: 'different'; caseId: string; differences: Difference[] }
  | { status: 'error'; caseId: string; stage: string; message: string };

async function compareLive(options): Promise<RunReport> { throw Error('not implemented'); }
function parseManifest(input): Cases { throw Error('not implemented'); }
async function observe(target, caseSpec, evidence): Promise<Observation> { throw Error('not implemented'); }
function parsePageData(body, caseSpec): Observation { throw Error('not implemented'); }
function differences(left, right): Difference[] { throw Error('not implemented'); }
```

`observe` owns URL construction, sequential GETs with timeout and redirects rejected, raw evidence, official devalue decoding, structural validation, identity resolution, and projection. Route-specific parsers own required fields; no generic recursive numeric coercion. Search uses `/search/__data.json?q=...`; members and independently resolved funders use their detail routes. Require correct model/result/status and unique exact selectors. Preserve search ordering, multiplicity, provenance, and identity context; omit only installation-local funder IDs. Verify selected detail identity after fetching it.

Project member declared totals, dates, completeness, counts and currency/category summaries; project organisation currency/party/recipient totals and counts. Preserve amount strings, nulls, missing-data semantics, and stable member identities. Canonicalize unordered breakdowns by semantic keys; preserve meaningful ranked arrays. Fail missing required fields rather than defaulting them. Comparison is pure structured equality with JSON-path diffs.

A fresh exclusive run directory contains request URL/status/body and timing, origins, observable build metadata, manifest, normalized observations, report JSON and readable diffs. Write initial metadata before requests and finalize report even after case failures. Never reuse a prior observation as a live result. Reject equal normalized origins before fetching. Production and development remain read-only.

This single operation hides protocol and evidence policy behind two meaningful caller inputs (boundary discipline); no adapter framework or generic schema engine is warranted.

## Synthesis decision

Independent candidate: recommend the HTTP/devalue design as the base.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- Accept a pinned decoder dependency for correct SvelteKit deserialization.
- Accept explicit financial projections for auditable coverage and fail-closed schema changes.
- Accept live data drift; differences require diagnosis, not automatic regression attribution.

## Alternatives considered

Browser DOM comparison hides transport but exposes selectors, rounded display amounts, hydration and browser setup; it cannot establish exact underlying financial equality. Manual Python decoding avoids npm but makes a framework serialization protocol our responsibility.

## Implementation reconciliation

No deviations yet.

## Open questions and risks

Which reachable development origin represents this branch? Missing access blocks live proof, not implementation or replay validation.

## Next implementation step

Implement page-data fixture replay with mutations proving ordered search, cross-database UUID independence, exact amounts, missing fields, ambiguous selectors and request failures cannot falsely pass; then run the live comparison.

# Cross-judge verdict

Scores assess the comparator design; all three need the lifecycle correction below before acceptance. Each criterion is 0–3.

| Candidate | Exact financial / ordered search / fail-closed schema | Public SvelteKit transport | Small skill-owned interface | Persisted evidence / errors | Independent entity identity | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Astra | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 15 |
| Sol | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 15 |
| Luna | 2 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 11 |

**Use Sol as the comparator base**, narrowly ahead of Astra because its projections explicitly cover recipient limit and its evidence contract includes partial-run markers, request metadata on transport failures, and incremental outcomes. Its exact direct devalue dependency, native Node implementation, and single script avoid redundant wrappers. Astra is also sound; borrow its explicit instruction to retain ranked-array order if clarifying which breakdowns are semantically ordered. Do not introduce sorting without grounding the actual loader contract: Sol's conservative preservation of array ordering is acceptable.

Luna adds a shell wrapper without a distinct responsibility, weakens funder selectors to name alone with normalized-name matching, and sketches member projections without category breakdowns or the full unknown/undated summary counts. Its final-write evidence shape is less explicit about preserving incomplete runs. Prefer Sol's query/name/funderKind selector with unique exact matching and independent per-origin UUID lookup. Both name and Parliament ID must be checked for MPs and recipient identities. Keep original UUIDs in raw evidence while excluding installation-local UUIDs from semantic equality.

**Mandatory lifecycle correction:** none of the candidates is acceptable as the complete verification workflow as written. The user's clarification requires launching this worktree's isolated Compose project with a database snapshot. Reject Sol's dismissal of snapshots, Astra's deletion of the refresh workflow insofar as it removes required snapshot preparation, and Luna's statement that no environment is launched. Retain live production as the comparison reference, replace monetary goldens with selectors, and keep snapshots as development provisioning input. The comparator may accept a development origin internally, but the default skill workflow must derive that origin from its worktree-specific Compose launch rather than accept an arbitrary existing deployment as branch proof.

Keep lifecycle orchestration in the existing skill/Compose mechanism where possible; do not add a pass-through shell wrapper around the Node comparator. Preserve comparison evidence outside resources removed during Compose cleanup. Parent should ground snapshot source, existing lifecycle machinery, and ownership before specifying provisioning commands; this verdict does not assume permission for imports into shared databases or stopping shared containers.

Minimum implementation acceptance: real-shaped envelope replay must catch changed exact money/null/count/completeness, missing required fields, search reorder/duplicates/provenance changes, ambiguous or missing identities, and transport/decode errors. Different funder UUIDs with equal independently verified identities must pass. Then run actual isolated snapshot-backed development versus live production, retaining raw and normalized evidence and treating differences as observed discrepancies rather than automatically attributing them to branch code.

name: verify
description: Compare selected Exposed searches and authoritative MP and organisation totals with live production, using an isolated snapshot-backed Compose build of the current worktree. Use after search, grouping, totals, or public loader changes.
---

# Verify against live production

Read [the feature map](features/README.md). From the repository root:

```sh
npm ci --prefix .agents/skills/verify
npm test --prefix .agents/skills/verify
./.agents/skills/verify/scripts/run-snapshot-comparison.sh
```

Require Docker Compose, Node with built-in fetch/test, curl, and an existing
`exposed_search_regression` snapshot in container `exposed-postgres-1` (user
`exposed`). Override those prerequisite identities with `VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_CONTAINER`,
`VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_DATABASE`, and `VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_USER` when necessary. The helper
can start a stopped source container and restores that initial state; it never
stops a source container that was already running. Do not run during snapshot
refresh. A missing snapshot is a failed prerequisite, never permission to ingest.
The [refresh helper](scripts/refresh-search-regression-db.sh) remains a separate,
deliberate replacement operation requiring its documented source-client shutdown.

The helper creates a unique project for this worktree/run, dumps one consistent
source snapshot, builds this worktree's backend/frontend with the production
Dockerfiles, and restores into its own PostgreSQL volume. Only that disposable
copy receives current migrations; checksum mismatches fail without alignment.
It does not rerun ingestion or refresh stored groups. The backend uses a read-only
connection; the frontend reaches its private API within the project's network.
No shared target/cache volumes or database ports are mounted. A random loopback
frontend port supplies the comparator's development origin. Doctor checks backend
health and decodes a successful public search model before comparison.

Production defaults to `https://exposed.today`. Every invocation reads it live
with bounded sequential GETs through the same SvelteKit page-data loaders used by
the public frontend. [The manifest](live-cases.json) contains selectors only,
never expected money. Resolve funder UUIDs independently in each environment by
one exact name/kind match, then assert the identity returned by each detail page.
Member Parliament IDs and names must match. Missing or ambiguous identities,
error models, malformed fields, redirects, HTTP failures and timeouts fail closed.

Compare supplied decimal strings/null without arithmetic, rounding, currency
conversion, or fallback totals. Search preserves order, duplicate multiplicity,
match provenance and entity context. Totals include authoritative declared periods,
counts/completeness, currencies/categories, parties and ranked recipients. Arrays
retain the public loader's order. Installation-local funder UUIDs are omitted only
from semantic comparisons; raw responses retain them.

The printed new evidence directory survives success, mismatch, failure and cleanup.
It records the worktree commit/dirty status, source container and snapshot, unique
Compose project, derived origin, build/migration/doctor/container/cleanup logs,
raw request URLs/status/headers/body/timestamps, normalized observations, incremental
`http/report.json`, and readable `http/diff.txt`. An interrupted comparator leaves
an incomplete report and available partial evidence. Treat incomplete evidence as
failure. Evidence includes a database dump; retain it according to local data policy.

Exit 0 requires every observation to succeed and match. Exit 1 means observed field
differences; exit 2 means observation/configuration/schema/identity errors (which
take precedence over differences). Report the code and evidence paths. Snapshot
age or live production changes can explain discrepancies, but discrepancies still
fail; investigate provenance before attributing them to branch code. Never edit
expected totals or refresh data to manufacture parity. There is no baseline-update
mode. The default snapshot currently predates grouped funder metadata, so missing
group identities can be valid observed errors.

Cleanup always removes only this run's Compose project and volumes, including on
failure. It retains the source snapshot and filesystem evidence. Check
`cleanup.log`; failed cleanup is exit 2. Do not use blanket Docker prune/down.

For controlled HTTP replay or diagnosis, the internal observer accepts explicit
origins; this alone does not prove a worktree build:

```sh
node .agents/skills/verify/scripts/compare-live.mjs --development http://127.0.0.1:PORT
```

Optional `--production ORIGIN`, `--cases PATH`, and `--evidence NEW_DIRECTORY` select
a controlled reference, selector subset, or evidence location. Equal origins are
rejected. The lifecycle command accepts only `--production` and `--cases`; it always
derives its own development origin and evidence directory. No production writes,
CI changes or financial-semantic changes are part of verification.
# Exposed live verification map

Run the snapshot-backed worktree comparison in [verify](../SKILL.md). The live
production loaders provide the comparison reference on every run. Selectors live
in [live-cases.json](../live-cases.json); none freeze monetary expectations.

- [Search](search.md): order, duplicates, identity context and match provenance.
- [MP totals](member-totals.md): John McDonnell and Alex Burghart.
- [Organisation totals](funder-totals.md): BBC, GB News, Premier League, HSBC and Unite.

This map covers selected public loader data. It does not verify rendered browser
interactions, ingestion resolution, or full declaration histories. Focused
application unit/integration tests remain separate checks. A historical snapshot
can legitimately differ from production; record those failures without altering
source data or claiming parity.

name: verify
description: Compare selected Exposed searches and authoritative MP and organisation totals with live production, using an isolated snapshot-backed Compose build of the current worktree. Use after search, grouping, totals, or public loader changes.
---

# Verify against live production

Read [the feature map](features/README.md). From the repository root:

```sh
npm ci --prefix .agents/skills/verify
npm test --prefix .agents/skills/verify
./.agents/skills/verify/scripts/run-snapshot-comparison.sh
```

Require Docker Compose, Node with built-in fetch/test, curl, and an existing
`exposed_search_regression` snapshot in container `exposed-postgres-1` (user
`exposed`). Override those prerequisite identities with `VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_CONTAINER`,
`VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_DATABASE`, and `VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_USER` when necessary. The helper
can start a stopped source container and restores that initial state; it never
stops a source container that was already running. Do not run during snapshot
refresh. A missing snapshot is a failed prerequisite, never permission to ingest.
The [refresh helper](scripts/refresh-search-regression-db.sh) remains a separate,
deliberate replacement operation requiring its documented source-client shutdown.

The helper creates a unique project for this worktree/run, dumps one consistent
source snapshot, builds this worktree's backend/frontend with the production
Dockerfiles, and restores into its own PostgreSQL volume. Only that disposable
copy receives current migrations; checksum mismatches fail without alignment.
It does not rerun ingestion or refresh stored groups. The backend uses a read-only
connection; the frontend reaches its private API within the project's network.
No shared target/cache volumes or database ports are mounted. A random loopback
frontend port supplies the comparator's development origin. Doctor checks backend
health and decodes a successful public search model before comparison.

Production defaults to `https://exposed.today`. Every invocation reads it live
with bounded sequential GETs through the same SvelteKit page-data loaders used by
the public frontend. [The manifest](live-cases.json) contains selectors only,
never expected money. Resolve funder UUIDs independently in each environment by
one exact name/kind match, then assert the identity returned by each detail page.
Member Parliament IDs and names must match. Missing or ambiguous identities,
error models, malformed fields, redirects, HTTP failures and timeouts fail closed.

Compare supplied decimal strings/null without arithmetic, rounding, currency
conversion, or fallback totals. Search preserves order, duplicate multiplicity,
match provenance and entity context. Totals include authoritative declared periods,
counts/completeness, currencies/categories, parties and ranked recipients. Arrays
retain the public loader's order. Installation-local funder UUIDs are omitted only
from semantic comparisons; raw responses retain them.

The printed new evidence directory survives success, mismatch, failure and cleanup.
It records the worktree commit/dirty status, source container and snapshot, unique
Compose project, derived origin, build/migration/doctor/container/cleanup logs,
raw request URLs/status/headers/body/timestamps, normalized observations, incremental
`http/report.json`, and readable `http/diff.txt`. An interrupted comparator leaves
an incomplete report and available partial evidence. Treat incomplete evidence as
failure. Evidence includes a database dump; retain it according to local data policy.

Exit 0 requires every observation to succeed and match. Exit 1 means observed field
differences; exit 2 means observation/configuration/schema/identity errors (which
take precedence over differences). Report the code and evidence paths. Snapshot
age or live production changes can explain discrepancies, but discrepancies still
fail; investigate provenance before attributing them to branch code. Never edit
expected totals or refresh data to manufacture parity. There is no baseline-update
mode. The default snapshot currently predates grouped funder metadata, so missing
group identities can be valid observed errors.

Cleanup always removes only this run's Compose project and volumes, including on
failure. It retains the source snapshot and filesystem evidence. Check
`cleanup.log`; failed cleanup is exit 2. Do not use blanket Docker prune/down.

For controlled HTTP replay or diagnosis, the internal observer accepts explicit
origins; this alone does not prove a worktree build:

```sh
node .agents/skills/verify/scripts/compare-live.mjs --development http://127.0.0.1:PORT
```

Optional `--production ORIGIN`, `--cases PATH`, and `--evidence NEW_DIRECTORY` select
a controlled reference, selector subset, or evidence location. Equal origins are
rejected. The lifecycle command accepts only `--production` and `--cases`; it always
derives its own development origin and evidence directory. No production writes,
CI changes or financial-semantic changes are part of verification.
# Exposed live verification map

Run the snapshot-backed worktree comparison in [verify](../SKILL.md). The live
production loaders provide the comparison reference on every run. Selectors live
in [live-cases.json](../live-cases.json); none freeze monetary expectations.

- [Search](search.md): order, duplicates, identity context and match provenance.
- [MP totals](member-totals.md): John McDonnell and Alex Burghart.
- [Organisation totals](funder-totals.md): BBC, GB News, Premier League, HSBC and Unite.

This map covers selected public loader data. It does not verify rendered browser
interactions, ingestion resolution, or full declaration histories. Focused
application unit/integration tests remain separate checks. A historical snapshot
can legitimately differ from production; record those failures without altering
source data or claiming parity.
"}}

Rebasing (1/3)Rebasing (2/3)Rebasing (3/3)Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/codex/prune-tests.
# Project summary and structure

The goal of this project is to make declaration data easy to search, browse and interpret.

- `exposed/` contains the rust application and CLI code that powers the project.
- `frontend/` contains a simple Svelte application
- `ingest/` contains the legacy Python scripts used to bootstrap this project.

## Exposed coding policy

- Follow with strict detail to the existing style of the application. This includes:
  - Type driven design
  - Domain modelling and parse-not-validate
  - Consistent error handling
  - Service layer abstractions

- Interactions with the database must use `sqlx` macros for compile-time query verification.

- For Rust changes, read and apply the
  [Rust domain development skill](.agents/skills/rust-domain-development/SKILL.md).
- Before implementation, identify the domain states, invariants, and the type
  that owns each rule. Parse external values into those types at boundaries and
  retain typed values internally.
- Use one canonical domain enum for each finite vocabulary. Do not duplicate
  its variants in string allowlists. Use exhaustive matches where behavior
  depends on a variant.
- When a bug exposes duplicated domain rules, remove the duplication rather
  than synchronizing the copies. Trace changes through producers, serialization,
  consumers, and persistence together.

## Financial totals contract

- The backend member summary owns mandatory declared GBP totals across all
  categories, including unknown category IDs. Frontends display those fields
  without recalculation or fallback sums.
- Current-term totals include records registered on or after
  `2024-07-09T00:00:00Z`. Historical totals include all records; undated records
  belong only to historical totals.
- Preserve exact decimal amounts and currencies. Do not convert currencies or
  pass amounts through JavaScript `Number`. Missing GBP amounts and unknown
  currencies make totals incomplete; known foreign currencies are excluded from
  GBP amounts without making totals incomplete.
- Preserve declaration counts and distinguish null amounts from zero. Label
  these as declared amounts, not earnings: declarations can include rates and
  benefits rather than money earned.
- Financial semantic changes require explicit user authorization and a description
  of their effects on included records/categories, currency, registration dates,
  missing values, precision, and labels. UI changes and refactoring must preserve
  these rules.

## Frontend coding policy

- Frontend presentation is largely a prototype. UI edits must preserve the financial contract above.

### Client and server

- Use Node.js 24+. From `frontend`, run `npm ci` and `npm run dev` for local
  development. Production uses `npm run build` followed by `node build`.
- Render initial page data through SvelteKit server loads. Keep Rust API access
  and response parsing in `frontend/src/lib/server` and `+page.server.ts`.
- Keep `EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN` on the server. Browser navigation and data requests
  go through the same-origin SvelteKit application, not directly to the Rust API.
- Pass typed, serializable page models to components. Keep browser APIs and SDK
  initialization in client hooks, event handlers, or `onMount` so SSR stays safe.
- Declare public configuration in `frontend/src/env.ts`. Use `dev` from
  `$app/env` for development-only behavior, including the design-system route.

### PostHog

- Initialize PostHog in `frontend/src/hooks.client.ts`, only outside development
  and when both public PostHog configuration values are present.
- Capture events in feature handlers, once per executed action. Preserve event
  names and property shapes for existing actions. Keep analytics out of shared UI
  components.
- Record metadata such as query length, entity type, and result position rather
  than raw search text or response payloads.
- Use `posthogLogger` for frontend diagnostic logs. Keep client error capture in
  the existing hook instead of adding duplicate exception reports.

### Design system

- Read the [component reference](frontend/src/lib/ui/README.md) and
  [composition recipes](frontend/src/lib/ui/COMPOSITION.md) before adding UI.
  The interactive reference is `/design-system` in development only.
- Import components and types from `frontend/src/lib/ui/index.ts` through the
  appropriate relative path. Load `frontend/src/lib/ui/styles.css` once in the
  root layout.
- Reuse components and typed variants. Use tokens for colors, spacing, and
  focus. Purple identifies MPs, teal identifies funders, and utility icons use
  the muted neutral color.
- Keep page arrangement, URLs, async work, and financial formatting in features.
  Shared UI accepts presentation models. Scope feature CSS to page arrangement
  and caller-authored content rather than component internals.
- Extend reusable patterns in `frontend/src/lib/ui`. Export public additions
  from the barrel, document their contracts, and add a gallery example. Cover
  changed behavior in `frontend/tests/design-system.spec.ts` or feature tests.

### UI verification

- Run `npm run check`, `npm run build`, and the affected Playwright tests from
  `frontend`. Gallery tests use a development server. Production tests use the
  built application.
- Every PR that changes the UI must include desktop screenshots in its
  description. Capture the affected views from the running application on
  the PR branch after completing the changes.
- Upload screenshots as GitHub attachments with `gh pr create --attach` or
  `gh pr edit --attach`. Use a GitHub CLI version that supports this flag. Never
  commit PR screenshots to the repository. Verify that the attachments render
  in the PR description before marking the PR ready for review.

## Ingest coding policy

- When porting code from this project, do not replicate the style. Use it as an end to end guide for functionality.

## Worktree policy

- For read-only tasks (investigating, reading, summarizing, or describing code),
  work on the current branch without creating a worktree.
- For tasks that require changing code or other files, work in a dedicated Git
  worktree before making changes. If a read-only task expands to require changes,
  switch to a dedicated worktree first.
- For such changes, reuse this chat's dedicated worktree if one already exists.
  Otherwise, create a sibling worktree with a unique branch and perform all
  edits, installs, and checks there.
- Never modify the primary checkout.
- Report the worktree path and branch when starting work in a dedicated worktree.

## Git history

- After completing and validating a task, commit its changes on the task's work
  branch without waiting for a separate request.
- Never commit directly on `main`.
- Keep Git history linear. Rebase feature branches onto the target branch and
  integrate changes with a fast-forward or squash; do not create merge commits.

## Development database migrations

- Keep schema changes in `db/migrations` as SQLx versioned `.up.sql` and
  `.down.sql` pairs. From the repository root, create a pair with
  `sqlx migrate add --source db/migrations --reversible <name>`.

set -euo pipefail
skill=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
VERIFY_WORKTREE=$(cd "$skill/../../.." && pwd)
export VERIFY_WORKTREE
if [ "$#" -eq 1 ] && [ "$1" = --help ]; then
  printf 'Usage: run-snapshot-comparison.sh [--production ORIGIN] [--cases PATH]\nLaunch this worktree in isolated snapshot-backed Compose; retain evidence and clean up own project.\n'
  exit 0
fi
args=("$@")
for ((i=0; i<${#args[@]}; i+=2)); do
  case "${args[i]}" in --production|--cases) ;; *) printf 'Expected --production ORIGIN or --cases PATH\n' >&2; exit 2;; esac
  [ $((i+1)) -lt ${#args[@]} ] || exit 2
done
source_container=${VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_CONTAINER:-exposed-postgres-1}
source_database=${VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_DATABASE:-exposed_search_regression}
source_user=${VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_USER:-exposed}
evidence=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/exposed-snapshot-comparison.XXXXXX")
project="exposed-verify-$(printf '%s' "$VERIFY_WORKTREE" | shasum | cut -c1-8)-$(date +%s)-$$"
compose=(docker compose -p "$project" -f "$skill/compose.yaml")
started_source=false
comparison_finished=false
# shellcheck disable=SC2329 # Invoked by the EXIT trap.
cleanup() {
  code=$?
  if [ "$code" -ne 0 ] && ! "$comparison_finished"; then code=2; fi
  trap - EXIT INT TERM
  "${compose[@]}" logs --no-color > "$evidence/compose.log" 2>&1 || true
  if "${compose[@]}" down --volumes --remove-orphans > "$evidence/cleanup.log" 2>&1; then
    printf 'removed own project %s\n' "$project" >> "$evidence/cleanup.log"
  else
    code=2
  fi
  if "$started_source"; then docker stop "$source_container" >> "$evidence/cleanup.log" 2>&1 || code=2; fi
  printf 'Evidence: %s\n' "$evidence"
  exit "$code"
}
trap 'cleanup' EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM
printf 'Evidence: %s\nProject: %s\n' "$evidence" "$project"
{
  printf 'worktree=%s\nproject=%s\nsource_container=%s\nsource_database=%s\nstarted_at=%s\n' "$VERIFY_WORKTREE" "$project" "$source_container" "$source_database" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  git -C "$VERIFY_WORKTREE" rev-parse HEAD

  docker inspect "$source_container" --format '{{.Id}} {{.State.Running}}'

fi

Verification needs to compare the current branch with live production while keeping a stable development dataset. Launch this worktree in its own Compose project from the existing database snapshot, then compare selected public search results and financial totals with https://exposed.today.

## What changed

- Add a skill-owned Compose lifecycle that copies the snapshot, migrates only the disposable copy, builds this worktree's backend/frontend, selects a loopback port, and removes its own containers and volumes after every run.
- Replace frozen expected-result JSON with query/entity selectors and a public SvelteKit loader comparator. Preserve exact decimal strings, counts, completeness, search order, and provenance; resolve organisation IDs separately in each environment. Retain raw responses, normalized values, diffs, and reports outside Compose resources.
- Prune redundant tests and move validation matrices into public parser/loader checks. Keep representative browser/process coverage, separate unit/browser commands, and retain the deliberate snapshot-refresh helper inside the skill.

## Scope

- Tests, the verification skill, and related documentation. CI and application financial/UI behavior are unchanged.
- Verification reads production and the source snapshot. It does not refresh source data, rerun ingestion, or alter production.

## Verification

- Six helper test groups, Svelte checks, Bash syntax, ShellCheck, skill validation, links, and Compose configuration pass. The frontend suite passes with two workers; the first parallel run had one gallery fixture-startup timeout that passed in isolation and on the full rerun.

- Actual isolated Compose runs proved exit 0 for matches, exit 1 for differences, and exit 2 for prerequisites/ambiguous identities. Each run retained evidence and removed its own project resources; the source snapshot retains its original migration history and row counts.

The snapshot differs from production. The full selection deliberately fails rather than accepting those differences or choosing an arbitrary GB News/Premier League row. Existing offline Rust test-query metadata remains incomplete; Rust validation used disposable PostgreSQL.

Validation matrices repeatedly launched browsers and CLI processes, and verification helpers lived outside their skill. Run those checks through the existing public parsers and loaders, and bundle the skill's helpers together.

## What changed

- Remove four redundant Rust tests, consolidate CLI parser/configuration matrices, and reuse parsed response schemas. Keep live Parliament checks opt-in with documented commands.
- Move malformed-response matrices into loader tests, share detail fixtures, merge repeated browser scenarios, and add separate unit/browser commands. Retain representative browser error and retry checks.

- Tests, verification helper packaging, and related documentation. Application behavior and CI are unchanged.
- Skill workflow expansion and startup-procedure repairs remain separate follow-ups.

- `npm --prefix frontend run check` reports no errors or warnings; `npm --prefix frontend test` passes all 95 tests. The unit command runs without an application build or browser.

- Relocated helpers retain identical success/failure replay output and evidence. Compose path/SQL checks use stubbed Docker without refreshing a database. Skill validation, executable permissions, and links pass.

Repository-wide frontend formatting still flags three unchanged files. Changed files are formatted. Rust test queries require online verification because the existing offline cache is incomplete.

Implemented in [PR #107](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/107).

The skill builds the current worktree in isolated Compose, restores a copy of the snapshot, and compares searches and exact totals with production. It preserves evidence and cleans up its containers and volumes.

```sh
npm ci --prefix .agents/skills/verify
./.agents/skills/verify/scripts/run-snapshot-comparison.sh
```

The live run found **8 matches, 5 differences, and 2 ambiguous organisations**. Both MPs, HSBC, and Unite totals matched. GB News and Premier League had multiple snapshot candidates.

All 110 frontend tests and six helper test groups pass. The source snapshot remains unchanged.

--- project-doc ---

# Project summary and structure

The goal of this project is to make declaration data easy to search, browse and interpret.

- `exposed/` contains the rust application and CLI code that powers the project.
- `frontend/` contains a simple Svelte application

## Worktree policy

- For read-only tasks (investigating, reading, summarizing, or describing code),
  work on the current branch without creating a worktree.
- For tasks that require changing code or other files, use [`worktrunk`](https://worktrunk.dev):
  - `wt switch --create <branch-name> --base main`
- Never modify the primary checkout without explicit permission.

## Exposed coding policy

- Follow with strict detail to the existing style of the application. This includes:
  - Type driven design
  - Domain modelling and parse-not-validate
  - Consistent error handling
  - Service layer abstractions

- Interactions with the database must use `sqlx` macros for compile-time query verification.

- For Rust changes, read and apply the
  [Rust domain development skill](.agents/skills/rust-domain-development/SKILL.md).
- Before implementation, identify the domain states, invariants, and the type
  that owns each rule. Parse external values into those types at boundaries and
  retain typed values internally.
- Use one canonical domain enum for each finite vocabulary. Do not duplicate
  its variants in string allowlists. Use exhaustive matches where behavior
  depends on a variant.
- When a bug exposes duplicated domain rules, remove the duplication rather
  than synchronizing the copies. Trace changes through producers, serialization,
  consumers, and persistence together.

## Financial totals contract

- The backend member summary owns mandatory declared GBP totals across all
  categories, including unknown category IDs. Frontends display those fields
  without recalculation or fallback sums.
- Current-term totals include records registered on or after
  `2024-07-09T00:00:00Z`. Historical totals include all records; undated records
  belong only to historical totals.
- Preserve exact decimal amounts and currencies. Do not convert currencies or
  pass amounts through JavaScript `Number`. Missing GBP amounts and unknown
  currencies make totals incomplete; known foreign currencies are excluded from
  GBP amounts without making totals incomplete.
- Preserve declaration counts and distinguish null amounts from zero. Label
  these as declared amounts, not earnings: declarations can include rates and
  benefits rather than money earned.
- Financial semantic changes require explicit user authorization and a description
  of their effects on included records/categories, currency, registration dates,
  missing values, precision, and labels. UI changes and refactoring must preserve
  these rules.

## Frontend coding policy

- Frontend presentation is largely a prototype. UI edits must preserve the financial contract above.

### Client and server

- Use Node.js 24+. From `frontend`, run `npm ci` and `npm run dev` for local
  development. Production uses `npm run build` followed by `node build`.
- Render initial page data through SvelteKit server loads. Keep Rust API access
  and response parsing in `frontend/src/lib/server` and `+page.server.ts`.
- Keep `EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN` on the server. Browser navigation and data requests
  go through the same-origin SvelteKit application, not directly to the Rust API.
- Pass typed, serializable page models to components. Keep browser APIs and SDK
  initialization in client hooks, event handlers, or `onMount` so SSR stays safe.
- Declare public configuration in `frontend/src/env.ts`. Use `dev` from
  `$app/env` for development-only behavior, including the design-system route.

### PostHog

- Initialize PostHog in `frontend/src/hooks.client.ts`, only outside development
  and when both public PostHog configuration values are present.
- Capture events in feature handlers, once per executed action. Preserve event
  names and property shapes for existing actions. Keep analytics out of shared UI
  components.
- Record metadata such as query length, entity type, and result position rather
  than raw search text or response payloads.
- Use `posthogLogger` for frontend diagnostic logs. Keep client error capture in
  the existing hook instead of adding duplicate exception reports.

### Design system

- Read the [component reference](frontend/src/lib/ui/README.md) and
  [composition recipes](frontend/src/lib/ui/COMPOSITION.md) before adding UI.
  The interactive reference is `/design-system` in development only.
- Import components and types from `frontend/src/lib/ui/index.ts` through the
  appropriate relative path. Load `frontend/src/lib/ui/styles.css` once in the
  root layout.
- Reuse components and typed variants. Use tokens for colors, spacing, and
  focus. Purple identifies MPs, teal identifies funders, and utility icons use
  the muted neutral color.
- Keep page arrangement, URLs, async work, and financial formatting in features.
  Shared UI accepts presentation models. Scope feature CSS to page arrangement
  and caller-authored content rather than component internals.
- Extend reusable patterns in `frontend/src/lib/ui`. Export public additions
  from the barrel, document their contracts, and add a gallery example. Cover
  changed behavior in `frontend/tests/design-system.spec.ts` or feature tests.

### UI verification

- Run `npm run check`, `npm run build`, and the affected Playwright tests from
  `frontend`. Gallery tests use a development server. Production tests use the
  built application.
- Every PR that changes the UI must include desktop screenshots in its
  description. Capture the affected views from the running application on
  the PR branch after completing the changes.
- Upload screenshots as GitHub attachments with `gh pr create --attach` or
  `gh pr edit --attach`. Use a GitHub CLI version that supports this flag. Never
  commit PR screenshots to the repository. Verify that the attachments render
  in the PR description before marking the PR ready for review.


## Git history

- After completing and validating a task, commit its changes on the task's work
  branch without waiting for a separate request.
- Never commit directly on `main`.
- Keep Git history linear. Rebase feature branches onto the target branch and
  integrate changes with a fast-forward or squash; do not create merge commits.

## Development database migrations

- Keep schema changes in `db/migrations` as SQLx versioned `.up.sql` and
  `.down.sql` pairs. From the repository root, create a pair with
  `sqlx migrate add --source db/migrations --reversible <name>`.
- Never change a migration file that existed before the current PR. Treat those
  migrations as immutable, even when they have not been applied locally.
- When a PR's schema design changes, you must edit, consolidate, or remove the
  migrations introduced by that PR. Do not append a corrective migration for an
  obsolete step in the same PR. Before review, the PR must contain only the
  migrations needed for its final schema. Recreate isolated test databases that
  applied a discarded PR migration; do not preserve obsolete steps just to
  satisfy their checksums.
- Do not fold changes into the baseline or put manual schema scripts in
  `db/upgrades`.
- From the repository root, apply migrations with
  `sqlx migrate run --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, inspect them with

# Project summary and structure

The goal of this project is to make declaration data easy to search, browse and interpret.

- `exposed/` contains the rust application and CLI code that powers the project.
- `frontend/` contains a simple Svelte application

## Worktree policy

- For read-only tasks (investigating, reading, summarizing, or describing code),
  work on the current branch without creating a worktree.
- For tasks that require changing code or other files, use [`worktrunk`](https://worktrunk.dev):
  - `wt switch --create <branch-name> --base main`
- Never modify the primary checkout without explicit permission.

## Exposed coding policy

- Follow with strict detail to the existing style of the application. This includes:
  - Type driven design
  - Domain modelling and parse-not-validate
  - Consistent error handling
  - Service layer abstractions

- Interactions with the database must use `sqlx` macros for compile-time query verification.

- For Rust changes, read and apply the
  [Rust domain development skill](.agents/skills/rust-domain-development/SKILL.md).
- Before implementation, identify the domain states, invariants, and the type
  that owns each rule. Parse external values into those types at boundaries and
  retain typed values internally.
- Use one canonical domain enum for each finite vocabulary. Do not duplicate
  its variants in string allowlists. Use exhaustive matches where behavior
  depends on a variant.
- When a bug exposes duplicated domain rules, remove the duplication rather
  than synchronizing the copies. Trace changes through producers, serialization,
  consumers, and persistence together.

## Financial totals contract

- The backend member summary owns mandatory declared GBP totals across all
  categories, including unknown category IDs. Frontends display those fields
  without recalculation or fallback sums.
- Current-term totals include records registered on or after
  `2024-07-09T00:00:00Z`. Historical totals include all records; undated records
  belong only to historical totals.
- Preserve exact decimal amounts and currencies. Do not convert currencies or
  pass amounts through JavaScript `Number`. Missing GBP amounts and unknown
  currencies make totals incomplete; known foreign currencies are excluded from
  GBP amounts without making totals incomplete.
- Preserve declaration counts and distinguish null amounts from zero. Label
  these as declared amounts, not earnings: declarations can include rates and
  benefits rather than money earned.
- Financial semantic changes require explicit user authorization and a description
  of their effects on included records/categories, currency, registration dates,
  missing values, precision, and labels. UI changes and refactoring must preserve
  these rules.

## Frontend coding policy

- Frontend presentation is largely a prototype. UI edits must preserve the financial contract above.

### Client and server

- Use Node.js 24+. From `frontend`, run `npm ci` and `npm run dev` for local
  development. Production uses `npm run build` followed by `node build`.
- Render initial page data through SvelteKit server loads. Keep Rust API access
  and response parsing in `frontend/src/lib/server` and `+page.server.ts`.
- Keep `EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN` on the server. Browser navigation and data requests
  go through the same-origin SvelteKit application, not directly to the Rust API.
- Pass typed, serializable page models to components. Keep browser APIs and SDK
  initialization in client hooks, event handlers, or `onMount` so SSR stays safe.
- Declare public configuration in `frontend/src/env.ts`. Use `dev` from
  `$app/env` for development-only behavior, including the design-system route.

### PostHog

- Initialize PostHog in `frontend/src/hooks.client.ts`, only outside development
  and when both public PostHog configuration values are present.
- Capture events in feature handlers, once per executed action. Preserve event
  names and property shapes for existing actions. Keep analytics out of shared UI
  components.
- Record metadata such as query length, entity type, and result position rather
  than raw search text or response payloads.
- Use `posthogLogger` for frontend diagnostic logs. Keep client error capture in
  the existing hook instead of adding duplicate exception reports.

### Design system

- Read the [component reference](frontend/src/lib/ui/README.md) and
  [composition recipes](frontend/src/lib/ui/COMPOSITION.md) before adding UI.
  The interactive reference is `/design-system` in development only.
- Import components and types from `frontend/src/lib/ui/index.ts` through the
  appropriate relative path. Load `frontend/src/lib/ui/styles.css` once in the
  root layout.
- Reuse components and typed variants. Use tokens for colors, spacing, and
  focus. Purple identifies MPs, teal identifies funders, and utility icons use
  the muted neutral color.
- Keep page arrangement, URLs, async work, and financial formatting in features.
  Shared UI accepts presentation models. Scope feature CSS to page arrangement
  and caller-authored content rather than component internals.
- Extend reusable patterns in `frontend/src/lib/ui`. Export public additions
  from the barrel, document their contracts, and add a gallery example. Cover
  changed behavior in `frontend/tests/design-system.spec.ts` or feature tests.

### UI verification

- Run `npm run check`, `npm run build`, and the affected Playwright tests from
  `frontend`. Gallery tests use a development server. Production tests use the
  built application.
- Every PR that changes the UI must include desktop screenshots in its
  description. Capture the affected views from the running application on
  the PR branch after completing the changes.
- Upload screenshots as GitHub attachments with `gh pr create --attach` or
  `gh pr edit --attach`. Use a GitHub CLI version that supports this flag. Never
  commit PR screenshots to the repository. Verify that the attachments render
  in the PR description before marking the PR ready for review.


## Git history

- After completing and validating a task, commit its changes on the task's work
  branch without waiting for a separate request.
- Never commit directly on `main`.
- Keep Git history linear. Rebase feature branches onto the target branch and
  integrate changes with a fast-forward or squash; do not create merge commits.

## Development database migrations

- Keep schema changes in `db/migrations` as SQLx versioned `.up.sql` and
  `.down.sql` pairs. From the repository root, create a pair with
  `sqlx migrate add --source db/migrations --reversible <name>`.
- Never change a migration file that existed before the current PR. Treat those
  migrations as immutable, even when they have not been applied locally.
- When a PR's schema design changes, you must edit, consolidate, or remove the
  migrations introduced by that PR. Do not append a corrective migration for an
  obsolete step in the same PR. Before review, the PR must contain only the
  migrations needed for its final schema. Recreate isolated test databases that
  applied a discarded PR migration; do not preserve obsolete steps just to
  satisfy their checksums.
- Do not fold changes into the baseline or put manual schema scripts in
  `db/upgrades`.
- From the repository root, apply migrations with
  `sqlx migrate run --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, inspect them with
  `sqlx migrate info --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, and revert the
  latest version with
  `sqlx migrate revert --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`.
  Commands read the root `.env`; set `DATABASE_URL` to select another database.
- SQLx owns each migration transaction. Do not add `BEGIN` or `COMMIT` to the
  migration files. Keep each down migration limited to its up migration's changes.
- Test forward upgrades with existing records and the full down/up cycle in an
  isolated database. Preserve imported data when upgrading an existing database.
- The one-time transition from the consolidated baseline requires schema and
  data verification before aligning its checksum. Follow `db/README.md`;
  changing the checksum alone does not apply schema changes.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.

If explicit user input is required for another reason before progress can safely continue, do not use the `request_user_input` tool. Ask the user directly with one concise plain-text question instead. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

---
name: fix-merge-conflicts
description: Resolve merge conflicts non-interactively, validate build and tests, and finalize conflict resolution
---

# Fix merge conflicts

## Trigger

Branch has unresolved merge conflicts and needs a reliable path to a buildable state.

## Workflow

1. Detect all conflicting files from git status and conflict markers.
2. Resolve each conflict with minimal, correctness-first edits.
3. Prefer preserving both sides when safe. Otherwise, choose the variant that compiles and keeps public behavior stable.
4. Regenerate lockfiles with package manager tools instead of hand-editing.
5. Run compile, lint, and relevant tests.
6. Stage resolved files and summarize key decisions.

## Guardrails

- Keep changes minimal and readable.
- Do not leave conflict markers in any file.
- Avoid broad refactors while resolving conflicts.
- Do not push or tag during conflict resolution.

## Output

- Files resolved
- Notable resolution choices
- Build/test outcome
# Codex tool mapping for pstack

pstack skills are written in Claude Code tool language (the `Skill` tool, the `Agent` tool, `AskUserQuestion`, Claude model names). On Codex the skills are the same files; only the tool names resolve differently. Read this when a pstack skill names a Claude tool, a driver or bundled skill, or a Claude model. This file is Codex-specific. Gemini CLI, opencode, Prime Agent, and other runtimes must use their own concrete tools, model names, and configuration paths.

## Tool actions

| pstack / Claude action | Codex equivalent |
|------------------------|------------------|
| Read a file | `shell` (`cat`, `head`, `tail`) |
| Create / edit / delete a file | `apply_patch` |
| Run a shell command | `shell` |
| Search file contents / find files | `shell` (`rg`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`) |
| Fetch a URL | `shell` with `curl` / `wget` |
| Search the web | `web_search` |
| Invoke a skill (the `Skill` tool, `/command`) | Skills load natively. Follow the instructions presented. |
| Dispatch a subagent (the `Agent`/`Task` tool) | `spawn_agent` |
| Dispatch N parallel subagents in one turn | N `spawn_agent` calls in one response |
| Wait for a subagent result | `wait_agent` |
| Free a finished subagent slot | `close_agent`, when the session exposes it. Some Codex hosts don't. |
| Track tasks (the todolist; `TaskCreate` / `TaskUpdate`, or `TodoWrite` on Claude Code) | `update_plan` |
| Ask the human a fixed-choice question (`AskUserQuestion`) | Ask in plain text and let the user answer. Codex has no structured-choice tool. |

Subagent dispatch needs `multi_agent` enabled. Add to `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[features]
multi_agent = true
```

Without it, `spawn_agent` is unavailable and the fan-out skills (`interrogate`, `why`, `how`, `arena`, `reflect`) degrade to a single sequential pass. A required independent review does not degrade. It stays blocked, as poteto-mode's [Subagents](../SKILL.md#subagents) section says.

Enabling `multi_agent` does not lift the host's thread limit. A thread-limit error from `spawn_agent` is a capacity error, not a rejected model slug, so the skills' fallback to another model does not apply. After the first capacity rejection, stop spawning. Close a finished agent with `close_agent` before you try again, and where the session has no `close_agent`, do not assume a finished agent's slot is free.

## Subagent policy

poteto-mode's Subagents section sets Claude-specific defaults (`subagent_type: "pstack:poteto-agent"`, `run_in_background: true`). On Codex:

- There is no `poteto-agent` subagent type. Route an ad-hoc subagent through poteto-mode's style by dispatching a `spawn_agent` whose instructions tell it to read the `poteto-mode` skill in full first.
- `spawn_agent` calls already run concurrently with your turn, so `run_in_background: true` has no separate flag. Issue the dispatch and continue.
- When a role value carries `@<level>`, or the `default effort` line names a level, pass that level as `spawn_agent`'s `reasoning_effort` and keep the dispatch otherwise unchanged. `session` passes no `reasoning_effort`.
- There is no `comment-sicko` subagent type either. The **no-comments** skill spawns it on Claude Code; on Codex dispatch a `spawn_agent` whose instructions tell it to read `poteto-mode/references/agents/comment-sicko.md` in full first.
- There are no `thermo-nuclear-review-subagent` or `thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review-subagent` types. The **thermos** skill spawns both on Claude Code; on Codex dispatch two `spawn_agent` calls whose instructions tell each to read the `thermo-nuclear-review` or `thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review` skill in full first and review only the diff and file contents in its prompt.
- Claude Code runs every subagent on this machine, so the **swarm** skill's workers and the fan-out playbooks (`orchestrate`, `autopilot-full`, `autopilot-stack`) isolate writers with worktrees. The same holds on Codex.
- Keep the rest of the policy unchanged. Pass file pointers not inlined context, give each worker its own worktree or branch when they write, review every subagent's diff yourself.

## Model names

Skills name Claude defaults (a single-role default for code/prose/judgment, a worker model for feature and refactoring code, plus a diverse-model panel for diverse-model panels; each model-consuming skill lists its own in a Models section). These slugs do not resolve on Codex. Substitute your configured Codex models:

- Single-model roles: your primary Codex model (for example `gpt-6-sol`).
- Roles that default to the Claude worker model (`feature, refactoring`): your fast Codex code model (for example `gpt-6-sol`).
- Roles that default to the strongest Claude model (`strongest judgment`): your strongest Codex model (for example `gpt-6-astra`).
- Diverse-model panels (`arena`, `architect`, `interrogate`, `how` critics, `reflect`): the adversarial signal comes from model diversity, so use the distinct Codex models available to you. A good default panel on ChatGPT is `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna`. If only one model family is reachable, vary reasoning effort and note in the verdict that diversity was reduced.

`/setup-pstack` writes the configured model list. On Codex, set it to your Codex model slugs.

## Session routing hook

The native pstack plugin bundles the same `SessionStart` routing instruction as the Claude Code plugin, through `session-start.sh` on macOS and Linux and `session-start.ps1` on Windows. Codex runs the hook on startup, resume, clear, and compact after the user trusts the hook through `/hooks`. The hook reads `session hook` from the Codex sheet, at the path in [setup-pstack's runtime table](../../setup-pstack/SKILL.md#other-runtimes); `session hook: off` disables injection.

A skills-only installation does not include plugin hooks. Request `poteto-mode` explicitly or add a standing instruction to `AGENTS.md` in that case.

The [driver policy](../SKILL.md#non-negotiables) selects the app driver. For skills and drivers named by these workflows, use these Codex equivalents:

`skills/poteto-mode/scripts/` ships the `watch-pr` PR watcher, the `orch` store CLI, and `worktree-audit.mjs`. Run `worktree-audit.mjs` with `node`, as its shebang does. The audit follows each link in a worktree's ancestor directories with `stat` and matches it by the directory it lands on, under bun and node alike. A worktree whose own path bun cannot resolve loses its last chat and lands in `review`. A dangling or looping link is ignored.
